scope: Validates the assignment metric this wrapper uses to align consecutive windows. It is a property of the tool integration, not an operating threshold: senselab ships unasdiff as a tool and does not tune its output, so no margin gate is defined here and none should be added. separate_with_unasdiff reports every window boundary's margin in metadata['unasdiff_alignment_margins'] as data; any decision built on those numbers belongs to the layer making the decision, with its own derivation, not to this file.
derivation: Measured via 200 trials, torch.manual_seed(0), 2000-sample synthetic signals: known-correct cases pair two independent randn(2000) sources with 5%-noise, cross-scaled copies of each other (0.8x and 1.2x) so exactly one assignment is right; ambiguous cases pair a single randn(2000) source with two near-identical 1%-noise copies of itself so no assignment is right. best_score - second_best_score over sorted(_assignment_scores(...)): known-correct p05/p50 = 1.93 / 2.00 (min 1.89, max 2.14); ambiguous p50/p95 = 2.3e-6 / 6.1e-6 (max 9.3e-6). The two distributions are separated by more than five orders of magnitude, which is what establishes that the scale-invariant correlation metric discriminates a real permutation swap from a genuine tie -- the property source_separation_test.py asserts. It says nothing about the margin distribution of real diffusion-sampled windows, and is not intended to: both categories are independent-Gaussian constructions.
history: v1 carried a 'first_real_measurements' field with two H100 margins (0.0109, 0.0579) from a 4.92 s clip, recorded as the start of a threshold calibration. Both were artifacts of a defect in this wrapper, not measurements of unasdiff: that clip is the case where _window_starts appends a final window flush against the end of the signal, overlapping its predecessor by more than hop_samples, while the alignment step sliced a fixed overlap_samples from each side. The two compared regions were therefore offset, and because the score is a dot product after normalisation, content shared at different indices contributes nothing -- so the margin measured the offset rather than the separation. Fixed by deriving the shared region per window pair; source_separation_test.py::test_irregular_final_window_aligns_on_its_true_shared_region reproduces the defective value (0.027) against the ~2.0 the same input yields once corrected. The field is gone rather than re-measured because fitting a gate is not part of including the tool.
